title: David Roddy Reported to Sign With Hapoel Jerusalem
dek: The 25-year-old forward, a 2022 first-round NBA pick, would make his first move outside the United States under new head coach Saša Obradović — though the deal has so far surfaced in only one report.

verificationSources.label: Wikipedia — David Roddy
Basketball-Reference — David Roddy
NBA.com — David Roddy
Wikipedia — Saša Obradović
Wikipedia — Jared Harper
Wikipedia — Hapoel Jerusalem B.C.

body: Hapoel Jerusalem has agreed to sign American forward David Roddy for next season, according to a report by the Israeli sports outlet ONE, in what would be the first move outside the United States of his professional career.

Per the report, Roddy's salary in Jerusalem is expected to approach $1 million for the season. Neither the club nor the player has commented publicly on the terms, and the length of the contract has not been disclosed.

Roddy, a 6-foot-5 forward out of Colorado State, was the No. 23 pick in the 2022 NBA Draft, selected by the Philadelphia 76ers before his rights were traded on draft night to the Memphis Grizzlies, where he began his professional career.

He has since played for the Grizzlies, Phoenix Suns, Atlanta Hawks and Philadelphia 76ers organizations, with additional time in the G League with the Memphis Hustle, the Suns' G League affiliate, Toronto Raptors 905 and the Grand Rapids Gold. His most recent NBA stop came with the Denver Nuggets, who signed him to a two-way contract on March 4, 2026.

The reported signing comes as Hapoel Jerusalem rebuilds under new head coach Saša Obradović, the veteran Serbian strategist who took over in June 2026 after a career that included stops with AS Monaco, Crvena Zvezda and ALBA Berlin. Guard Jared Harper, the reigning Israeli Premier League and EuroCup MVP, is among the few holdovers as the club overhauls its roster of imports.

Jerusalem is one of Israeli basketball's most decorated clubs and has been active in the free-agent market this offseason as it looks to build a squad capable of competing deep into next season's EuroCup.

As of publication, the agreement had been reported by only one outlet. Hapoel Jerusalem's official channels and other Israeli and international outlets had not yet confirmed the signing, and further details, including contract length, remain unverified.

Roddy's salary in Jerusalem is reported to be close to $1 million for the season; the contract length has not been disclosed.

He played college basketball at Colorado State and has since appeared for the Grizzlies, Suns, Hawks and 76ers organizations, signing a two-way contract with the Denver Nuggets on March 4, 2026.

Guard Jared Harper, the reigning Israeli Premier League and EuroCup MVP, remains on Hapoel Jerusalem's roster.
The move to Jerusalem would be Roddy's first professional stint outside the United States, according to the report.
As of publication, only one outlet had reported the signing, and it had not been independently confirmed by other Israeli or international media.

title: Mamo and Mantel Break Israeli Records at National Athletics Championships
dek: Noam Mamo ran 46.58 seconds in the 400m and Yarden Mantel cleared 4.16 meters in the pole vault, each improving marks they had set only weeks earlier, on a record-setting day at Israel's national athletics championships in Jerusalem.

verificationSources.label: World Athletics athlete profile — Noam Mamu
Hebrew Wikipedia — Yarden Mantel
Hebrew Wikipedia — Noam Mamo
Israel Athletics Association — recent Israeli records recap

body: Two Israeli athletics records fell on the same day at Givat Ram Stadium in Jerusalem on Monday, as sprinter Noam Mamo and pole vaulter Yarden Mantel both bettered marks they had set only weeks earlier during the national championships.

Mamo won the men's 400m in 46.58 seconds, shaving two-tenths off the Israeli record of 46.78 seconds he had set just four days earlier at a meet in Liège, Belgium. World Athletics lists that Liège clocking, from July 15, as his official personal best entering the championships, making Monday's run his second national record inside a week.

The time continues a rapid rise for Mamo, who has cut more than a second off the Israeli 400m mark over the past four years, moving from 47.63 seconds in 2022 to 47.57 in 2023 and 46.82 last year before this month's back-to-back improvements. He also holds Israel's national record in the 800m.

In the pole vault, Mantel cleared 4.16 meters to add a centimeter to the Israeli U20 and U23 record of 4.15 meters she had set in January. The height kept her progression intact after a season in which she has repeatedly pushed her own national mark higher.

"I'm happy things came together for me, but I feel I haven't yet shown all my abilities," Mantel said after her winning vault, signaling she expects to add to the record again before the season is out.

Monday's session was part of Israel's 90th national athletics championships, a fixture on the Israel Athletics Association calendar that regularly serves as the proving ground where the country's junior and senior record books are rewritten.

With both records now in the books, attention turns to whether Mamo and Mantel can carry the form into international competition later this year, after a championship day that underlined the depth of young talent currently coming through Israeli athletics.

Mamo's previous Israeli record of 46.78 seconds was set four days earlier, on July 15, 2026, at a meet in Liège, Belgium, per his World Athletics profile.
Mamo also holds Israel's national 800m record, according to the Israel Athletics Association.
Yarden Mantel cleared 4.16 meters in the pole vault, breaking her own Israeli U20/U23 record of 4.15 meters, which she had set in January 2026.
Mantel said after the competition: "I'm happy things came together for me, but I feel I haven't yet shown all my abilities."
The championships were held at Givat Ram Stadium in Jerusalem.

title: Messi: 'The Pain Is Enormous' After World Cup Final Heartbreak
dek: In his first public comments since Spain's extra-time win, Lionel Messi called Argentina's 1-0 defeat devastating but said the run to consecutive finals was something to hold onto.

verificationSources.label: ESPN
NBC News
CBS Sports
ABC News
FIFA official match centre
Yahoo Sports (red card detail)

body: Hours after Argentina's World Cup dream ended in extra time, Lionel Messi broke his silence. In his first public comments since Spain's 1-0 win in the final at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey, the Argentine captain posted a message on Instagram acknowledging the scale of the disappointment while insisting the campaign still had much to be proud of.

"The pain is enormous, and it will take time for this wound to heal," Messi wrote. "But I also hold onto all the good things." The post marked his first reaction to a result that denied Argentina back-to-back titles and instead handed Spain its second World Cup crown, and its first since 2010.

The final itself was settled deep into extra time. Neither side broke through across a scoreless 90 minutes, and it was not until the 106th minute that Ferran Torres struck the decisive goal, sending Spain's bench into celebration and closing out a tournament in which the team never trailed.

Argentina were already fighting the result shorthanded. Midfielder Enzo Fernández was sent off in the 93rd minute, picking up a second yellow card for a collision with Spain defender Pau Cubarsí, and Argentina played the entirety of extra time a man down as they searched for a way back into the match.

In the rest of his message, Messi said it was still difficult to fully process what the squad had achieved. "It's hard to appreciate today what we did, but this group reached two consecutive World Cup finals," he wrote, adding that the run had again brought the country together. He also offered congratulations to Spain on the title.

The defeat carries particular weight given the timeline of Messi's career. Having lifted the trophy in 2022 after Argentina beat France on penalties, he returned four years later chasing an unprecedented repeat. He will be 43 by the time the 2030 World Cup is played, and Sunday's final is widely regarded as his last appearance on football's biggest stage.

For Spain, the triumph completes a tournament defined by control rather than spectacle, with the team conceding little and grinding out the final without ever surrendering a shot on target to Argentina. The champions' celebrations at MetLife Stadium closed out the first World Cup jointly hosted across the United States, Mexico and Canada.
facts: Spain beat Argentina 1-0 in extra time to win the 2026 World Cup final on July 19, 2026, at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey.
Ferran Torres scored the only goal of the match in the 106th minute of extra time.
Argentina's Enzo Fernández was sent off in the 93rd minute for a second yellow card after a collision with Spain's Pau Cubarsí, leaving Argentina to play all of extra time with ten men.
The win gave Spain its second World Cup title, and its first since 2010.
Lionel Messi posted his first reaction on Instagram after the loss, writing that 'the pain is enormous' and that it would 'take time for this wound to heal.'
The final was Argentina's second consecutive World Cup final appearance, after winning the title in 2022.
Messi, who will be 43 by the 2030 World Cup, is widely expected to have played his last World Cup match.

title: FIFA to Weigh Expanding 2030 World Cup to 64 Teams
dek: A CONMEBOL-backed plan to mark the World Cup's centenary with 64 nations is under formal review at FIFA, a shift that could also reshape Europe's — and Israel's — qualifying path.

verificationSources.label: ESPN
Sky Sports
Al Jazeera
Wikipedia — 2030 FIFA World Cup
Walla Sport (Israeli angle)
Sport1 (Maariv, Israeli angle)

body: FIFA has confirmed it will formally examine a proposal to expand the 2030 World Cup from 48 to 64 teams, reviving an idea first pushed by South American confederation CONMEBOL as a one-off tribute to the tournament's centenary.

FIFA president Gianni Infantino said discussion of the expansion would begin now that the 2026 World Cup, hosted by the United States, Canada and Mexico, has concluded. He stressed that no decision has been made and that FIFA's council has a duty to formally consider any proposal referred to it by member federations.

The plan originated with CONMEBOL president Alejandro Domínguez, who has described a 64-team format as his personal dream for marking 100 years since the inaugural World Cup was staged in Uruguay in 1930. Domínguez met Infantino, along with the presidents of Argentina, Paraguay and Uruguay, in New York to press the case directly.

The 2030 tournament is currently scheduled to run under the same 48-team format introduced at the 2026 finals, co-hosted by Spain, Portugal and Morocco. As part of the centenary celebrations, single commemorative matches are planned for Montevideo's Estadio Centenario, Buenos Aires and Asunción, honoring the three South American nations that staged the first edition.

Under the format being studied, the tournament would be restructured into 16 groups of four teams, with the top two from each advancing to a 32-team knockout stage — doubling the total number of matches to 128. UEFA president Aleksander Čeferin has publicly opposed the idea, calling it "not a good idea," and the international players' union has raised separate concerns about an already congested qualifying calendar and player welfare.

The plan carries a speculative Israeli sporting angle. Commentary in the Israeli press has pointed to an associated proposal that would lift Europe's qualifying allocation to roughly 21 berths, up from 16 at the 2026 finals, as a change that could improve the national team's prospects of returning to the World Cup for the first time since 1970. That calculation remains provisional, since UEFA has not drafted, let alone approved, a qualifying format for an expanded tournament.

For now, FIFA has framed the 64-team idea as one option under review rather than a settled outcome, with officials cautioning that no timeline exists for a final decision. Any change to the 2030 format would require sign-off from FIFA's council, and given entrenched opposition from UEFA and players' representatives, observers expect a prolonged debate before Uruguay, Argentina, Paraguay, Spain, Portugal and Morocco learn the exact shape of the tournament they are set to host.
facts: CONMEBOL formally proposed expanding the 2030 World Cup from 48 to 64 teams as a one-off centenary celebration, first raised at a March 2025 FIFA Council meeting.
FIFA president Gianni Infantino said in July 2026, after the 2026 World Cup concluded, that FIFA will formally examine the 64-team proposal for 2030; FIFA has stressed no decision is imminent.

The 2030 World Cup is currently scheduled as a 48-team tournament co-hosted by Spain, Portugal and Morocco, with centenary matches in Montevideo, Buenos Aires and Asunción marking 100 years since the first World Cup in Uruguay.
Under the proposed 64-team format, the tournament would expand to 16 groups of four teams, with the top two advancing to a 32-team knockout stage, doubling the match count to 128.
UEFA president Aleksander Čeferin has publicly opposed the plan, and the global players' union has raised concerns about the qualifying calendar and player welfare.

Israeli sports commentary has linked the proposal to a possible expansion of Europe's qualifying slots to around 21, which could improve Israel's chances of reaching the World Cup for the first time since 1970 — an estimate not yet confirmed by UEFA.

title: Hapoel Nof HaGalil Rebuilds Youth Coaching Staff After Relegation
dek: A new professional manager and a reshuffled panel of junior-team coaches aim to stabilize the club's academy following the senior side's drop to Liga Aleph.

verificationSources.label: Goler1 report on Roei Cohen's role as Hapoel Nof HaGalil professional manager
Hebrew Wikipedia entry on Giorgi Daraselia
English Wikipedia entry on Hapoel Nof HaGalil F.C.

body: Hapoel Nof HaGalil is rebuilding its youth coaching staff this summer, moving to steady an academy that had been left in limbo while the club sorted out its senior-team direction following relegation from Liga Leumit to Liga Aleph at the close of the 2025/26 season.

At the head of the reshuffle is Roei Cohen, who has been installed as the club's professional manager. Cohen arrives with experience in the same role at M.S. Kfar Qasem and at Hapoel Kfar Saba in the National League, and his appointment is intended to give the academy a clearer chain of command after a period of uncertainty tied to the senior team's fall.

Giorgi Daraselia, the Georgian-born former midfielder who has held administrative roles in the club's youth setup since 2022, remains closely involved with the department. Daraselia, who played for Hapoel Tel Aviv and other Israeli sides after arriving from Georgia in the late 1990s and later helped Maccabi Haifa to league titles as part of its coaching staff, is reported to be taking on direct coaching duties with the age group born in 2010.

Islam Kanaan continues in his post overseeing the club's youth coaching, staying on to work with the age group born in 2009 — the cohort that won a northern regional championship this past season, a result the club is hoping to build on as several of those players move up through the ranks.

Gabi Mistatski is returning to coach the 2011 age group, a reappointment the club has framed as a vote of continuity for a coach already familiar with the squad, while Shachar Poni joins the staff to take charge of a younger junior group, bringing experience gained coaching youth sides elsewhere in the north.

The appointments matter beyond the academy's internal bookkeeping: Israeli lower-league clubs typically depend on a functioning youth pipeline to offset the financial strain of relegation, and a settled coaching panel is often the first visible sign that a club's off-field affairs have stabilized after a difficult season.

The changes were reported by the club's channels and by ONE; the precise scope of each coach's mandate for the 2026/27 season, including exact league placements for every junior squad, had not yet been independently detailed by other outlets at the time of writing, and should be treated as provisional pending further confirmation.

Roei Cohen has been appointed professional manager of Hapoel Nof HaGalil, having previously held the same role at M.S. Kfar Qasem and Hapoel Kfar Saba.
Giorgi Daraselia, a Georgian-born former player who has worked in the club's youth administration since 2022, is reported to be coaching the age group born in 2010.
Islam Kanaan continues overseeing the club's youth coaching and works with the 2009 age group, which won a northern regional championship.
Gabi Mistatski is returning to coach the 2011 age group, and Shachar Poni has joined the staff to coach a younger junior group.

title: Hapoel Tel Aviv's Road to Europe Runs Through Bulgaria, With Žilina or Katowice Waiting
dek: Before any thought of a third qualifying round, Hapoel Tel Aviv must first get past Bulgaria's Ludogorets Razgrad in the Conference League's second round.

verificationSources.label: UEFA.com – Ludogorets vs H. Tel-Aviv match page

body: Hapoel Tel Aviv's return to European competition begins in earnest this week, with a second qualifying round tie against Bulgaria's Ludogorets Razgrad standing between the Reds and a rare tilt at the UEFA Conference League's third qualifying round. Should Hapoel advance, the reward is a meeting with the winner of a parallel tie between Slovakia's MŠK Žilina and Poland's GKS Katowice, whose paths to this stage were shaped by their own European campaigns earlier in the summer.

The first leg against Ludogorets is scheduled for Thursday, July 23, in Tel Aviv, with the return fixture set for July 30 at Ludogorets' Huvepharma Arena in Razgrad. Ludogorets arrive as a club still adjusting to a changed domestic landscape: after fourteen consecutive Bulgarian championships, their title run was ended this season by Levski Sofia, which sealed the 2025-26 crown in early May. The Bulgarian side remains one of the country's most experienced European campaigners regardless of the shift at home.

Hapoel Tel Aviv's presence in the qualifying rounds at all reflects a rapid turnaround domestically. The club, newly returned to the top flight of Israeli football, finished fourth in last season's championship playoffs, a result that was enough to secure a continental berth via the Conference League path.

Waiting in the wings, contingent on results over the next ten days, are Žilina and Katowice, who play their own second qualifying round tie on the same two dates, July 23 and July 30. Žilina reached this stage after a bruising Europa League exit: the Slovak club had entered continental competition as reigning Slovak Cup winners, having beaten FC Košice 3-1 in the final in May, but fell 3-2 on aggregate to Croatia's Hajduk Split in the first qualifying round, winning the first leg before a heavier second-leg defeat sent them down the UEFA ladder into the Conference League.

Katowice's route was more straightforward. A fifth-place finish in the Polish Ekstraklasa, sealed on the final day of the season with a 1-1 draw against Pogoń Szczecin that overtook Legia Warsaw in the standings, was enough for continental qualification. It marks the Silesian club's return to Europe after a 23-year absence rather than a debut on the continental stage — Katowice previously featured in the old European Cup Winners' Cup and UEFA Cup between 1970 and 2003, including ties against Barcelona, Rangers, Benfica and Galatasaray.

Both sets of Slovak and Polish observers regard Žilina as the likelier of the two to advance, pointing to the Slovak club's deeper recent European pedigree relative to a Katowice side still finding its footing on the continental stage after such a long absence. Nothing is decided, however, until the two legs are played out over the coming week and a half.

For now, the immediate task in Tel Aviv is Ludogorets, and Hapoel's coaching staff have been careful not to look beyond a tie against a club with genuine European experience even in a transitional season. A result across the two legs against the Bulgarians remains the only thing standing between Hapoel Tel Aviv and a third qualifying round assignment against one of two contrasting European sides — one steeped in continental football, the other rediscovering it after more than two decades away.
facts: Hapoel Tel Aviv face Ludogorets Razgrad in the UEFA Conference League second qualifying round: first leg July 23 in Tel Aviv, return leg July 30 in Razgrad.

The winner of the Hapoel–Ludogorets tie advances to a third qualifying round meeting with the winner of MŠK Žilina (Slovakia) vs GKS Katowice (Poland), who play their second-round tie on the same two dates.

Žilina reached the Conference League after losing 3-2 on aggregate to Hajduk Split in the Europa League first qualifying round, having entered Europe as 2025-26 Slovak Cup winners (3-1 over FC Košice in the final).

GKS Katowice qualified for Europe by finishing fifth in the 2025-26 Polish Ekstraklasa; this is a return to continental competition after a 23-year absence, not a debut — the club last played in Europe in 2003 after Cup Winners' Cup and UEFA Cup appearances dating back to 1970.
Hapoel Tel Aviv qualified for the Conference League by finishing fourth in the Israeli Premier League playoffs after returning to the top division.
Ludogorets Razgrad's run of fourteen consecutive Bulgarian league titles ended in the 2025-26 season, with Levski Sofia crowned champions in early May 2026.

body: Two Israeli match officials have been entrusted with fixtures in the opening qualifying rounds of Europe's second- and third-tier club competitions, according to a report published this week in the Israeli press. David Fuksman and Snir Levi will each take charge of a second qualifying-round tie, extending Israel's presence on the continental refereeing stage even as the game's international politics remain fraught.

Fuksman has been assigned a UEFA Conference League qualifier between the Romanian side commonly known as Steaua Bucharest — competing under the name FCSB — and the Latvian club Auda of Riga. The reported fixture matches UEFA's published second qualifying-round pairing of FCSB and Auda, whose two legs are scheduled for 23 and 30 July 2026, with the first leg staged in Bucharest.

Levi, for his part, is listed to officiate a UEFA Europa League qualifier between the Norwegian club Tromso and the Czech side Hradec Kralove. The competition record confirms the two teams were drawn together in the Europa League second qualifying round, with the first leg at Tromso's Romssa Arena on 23 July and the return in Hradec Kralove on 30 July 2026.

The original report also named accompanying crews of assistant referees expected to travel with each official, framing the appointments as Israeli representatives who would serve through the summer rounds. The identities of the two centre officials check out against public refereeing records: Fuksman and Levi both appear in international match-official databases with prior European and Israeli top-flight assignments.

The rounds and the club pairings are independently corroborated by UEFA's own match listings and the tournament qualifying records. What could not be independently confirmed from UEFA's public pages at the time of writing were the referee appointments themselves, which rest on the single Israeli-language report and, in Levi's case, a secondary refereeing-statistics entry pointing to the same tie.

The assignments arrive against a charged backdrop, with Israeli clubs and officials continuing to feature in UEFA competitions amid periodic debate over their participation. For the Israel Football Association's refereeing department, appointments to cross-border ties in the qualifying phase are a familiar route by which its officials build the record needed for higher-profile group-stage and knockout work.

Until UEFA formally publishes its officiating list for each leg, the specific match, leg and kick-off for each referee should be read as attributed to the reporting rather than confirmed by the governing body. The competition, round and clubs, however, align cleanly with the official calendar for the second qualifying rounds of both the Europa League and the Conference League.

Snir Levi is reported to referee a UEFA Europa League second qualifying-round tie between Norway's Tromso and Czech side Hradec Kralove.

body: Blessing Afrifah, the sprinter who holds Israel's national 100m record, has been pulled at the last moment from both the 100m and the 200m at the national athletics championships in Jerusalem after a hamstring injury.

The report said that Afrifah, troubled by the hamstring for several weeks, was struck from the entry lists shortly before the meeting at the Givat Ram stadium, with the medical staff judging it safer to rest him than to risk aggravating the muscle.

Afrifah is the fastest man Israel has produced. He set the national 100m record of 10.09 seconds in Jerusalem in July 2025, ending a mark that had stood for more than two decades, and he also owns the national 200m record of 19.96, run as a teenager in 2022.

Now 22, he won the 200m at the 2022 World Under-20 Championships and took the European Under-23 title in both 2023 and 2025, and he had been the defending champion in both sprints at these national championships.

The decision to hold him back is tied to the calendar: by the report's account the European Athletics Championships in Birmingham are only about a month away, and his team preferred to protect his fitness for the continental stage rather than chase domestic titles at home.

The withdrawal also lands on a weekend already heavy with meaning for Israeli athletics, marking as it does the close of decathlon record-holder Ariel Atias's competitive career, whose retirement this desk reported separately.

No return date has been given, and for now the withdrawal rests on a single Israeli report; his condition in the run-up to Birmingham is likely to become the more telling measure of how serious the injury proves to be.
facts: Blessing Afrifah was withdrawn at the last moment from the 100m and 200m at the Israeli Athletics Championships in Jerusalem (Givat Ram) with a hamstring injury, according to the source report.

He also holds the national 200m record of 19.96 (2022) and was 200m champion at the 2022 World U20 Championships and the 2023 and 2025 European U23 Championships.

The same weekend marked the retirement of decathlon record-holder Ariel Atias, covered separately by this desk.

body: Maccabi Tel Aviv are on the verge of adding to their attack, with Israeli reports on Monday indicating that the club have reached a principle agreement to sign Slovenian striker Ester Sokler from Serbian side Radnicki 1923. The framework of the transfer is said to be settled between the two clubs, though the player has not yet put pen to paper and the move should not be treated as complete.

According to the Israeli coverage, the fee involved is in the region of one million euros. That would represent a substantial return for Radnicki, who only turned Sokler's loan from Aberdeen into a permanent transfer in January 2026, and it reflects the impact the forward made across the second half of the Serbian SuperLiga campaign.

The reporting describes the deal as roughly ninety-five per cent complete, with those close to the negotiations expecting matters to be finalised within about forty-eight hours. Israeli outlets have also indicated that Sokler's wages would be upgraded on the terms he holds in Serbia, with figures of around 200,000 to 250,000 euros a year cited, although those numbers have not been formally confirmed by either club.

Sokler, who turned 27 in June, enjoyed the most productive season of his career in 2025-26. Across his loan and permanent spells with Radnicki he registered 15 goals in 29 league appearances, a tally that helped the Kragujevac club preserve their top-flight status after a difficult campaign. That scoring rate is understood to have made him a priority target for Maccabi's recruitment staff.

A native of Krsko in eastern Slovenia, the striker came through at NK Krsko before spells with Brezice, Celje and Radomlje. He moved to Scotland with Aberdeen in the summer of 2023, where he spent close to three seasons and won the 2025 Scottish Cup, before the loan to Serbia reignited his form in front of goal.

At international level Sokler is a recent addition to the senior picture rather than an established name. He earned his first cap for Slovenia in June 2026, coming off the bench in a 1-1 draw with Cyprus, and remains uncapped beyond that single appearance as he looks to build on his breakout club season.

Should the transfer be completed as expected, Sokler would arrive as a central striking option and a reported priority of Maccabi's new sporting leadership. Other clubs, including Sweden's Malmo and Serbia's Partizan Belgrade, were said to have monitored his situation, but for now the momentum is firmly with the Israeli champions. Until the signature is confirmed, however, the deal stays in the advanced-but-pending category.

He has one senior Slovenia cap, debuting in June 2026 as a substitute in a 1-1 draw with Cyprus.

body: A tearful Lionel Scaloni left his press conference early in East Rutherford on Sunday night, saying Argentina's 1-0 World Cup final defeat to Spain "hurts me in the soul" and committing only to seeing out his contract, which expires in December, before deciding whether to continue as national team coach.

Ferran Torres's goal in the 106th minute of extra time settled the final and ended Argentina's bid to become the first side since Brazil in 1962 to retain the trophy. Enzo Fernández was sent off late in regulation, leaving the holders to chase the game a man down.

Asked directly about his future, Scaloni stopped short of a resignation. "I will complete my contract and then see," he said. "I will talk with the president, but I more or less have an idea of what I want to do. Honestly, I feel the need to think, because I don't know if we'll be able to do something as grand as this."

The 48-year-old struggled to hold his composure as the questions continued. "Bear with me, I don't know if I can continue," he said, before standing up, apologising — "It's really painful, I am very sorry" — and walking out to applause from the Argentine journalists in the room.

He offered a glimpse of how heavy another cycle would feel. "In order to continue you need a great deal of things, especially resetting your mind, rebooting, creating a group like this again," he said, adding that the likely first step was "to relax and to stop for a bit".

Scaloni has led Argentina since 2018, when he took over on an interim basis after a chastening tournament in Russia. He rebuilt the squad around Lionel Messi and delivered the Copa América in 2021 — ending a 28-year title drought — the 2022 World Cup in Qatar and a second Copa América in 2024.

His deal with the Argentine federation runs to the end of 2026, and a decision is expected only after he sits down with president Claudio Tapia. For now, the coach who restored Argentina to the top of the world game has promised nothing beyond December — and made no secret of how much Sunday cost him.
facts: Spain beat Argentina 1-0 after extra time in the World Cup final on 19 July 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey; Ferran Torres scored in the 106th minute.
Scaloni on the defeat: "Losing hurts me in the soul."
On his future: "I will complete my contract and then see" — the deal expires in December 2026; no explicit resignation was announced.
He left the press conference in tears, apologising, and was applauded out of the room by Argentine media.
Scaloni has coached Argentina since 2018, winning the Copa América in 2021 and 2024 and the 2022 World Cup.
A final decision is expected after talks with federation president Claudio Tapia.

title: Kings of the world: Ferran Torres strikes in extra time as Spain beat Argentina 1-0 to win the 2026 World Cup
dek: The European champions suffocated Lionel Messi's Argentina at MetLife Stadium, survived Emiliano Martinez's record 11 saves and a disallowed goal, and won their second World Cup through Ferran Torres' 106th-minute volley — while more than 10,000 Israelis watched together at Menora Mivtachim Hall in Tel Aviv.

source.name: ESPN
source.originalTitle: Spain edge Argentina after extra time to win 2nd World Cup title
source.author: Mark Ogden

verificationSources.label: ESPN — Gamecast: full-time status, lineups, statistics, referee

body: Spain are champions of the world. On a heavy summer night at MetLife Stadium, the European champions beat Argentina 1-0 after extra time to win the 2026 World Cup, their second star arriving sixteen years after their first. It took 106 minutes, a red card, a disallowed goal and the finest goalkeeping display a final has ever seen before Ferran Torres, a 62nd-minute substitute, finally broke Argentina — volleying into the roof of the net after Nico Williams headed Pedro Porro's cross into his path.

For 90 minutes the pattern never wavered. Spain passed, probed and pinned Argentina into their own third, finishing with 65 per cent of possession and 20 shots to Argentina's two; the holders did not manage a single shot on target all night, a statistic without precedent in a World Cup final of the modern era. That it remained goalless so long was down to one man: Emiliano Martinez, whose 11 saves were the most ever recorded in a World Cup final, according to figures carried by ESPN and the Associated Press.

The match turned in stoppage time of the 90. Enzo Fernandez, booked in the 82nd minute for dissent, launched into a reckless challenge that sent Pau Cubarsi somersaulting, and Slovenian referee Slavko Vincic showed the Chelsea midfielder a second yellow card in the third added minute. The decision was widely reported as justified, and it condemned Argentina to face half an hour of extra time with ten tired men against the deepest squad in the tournament.

Even then Argentina were reprieved twice. Martinez clawed away a Williams effort in the 93rd minute, and when Williams did put the ball in the net early in extra time, the goal was ruled out for a foul on Nicolas Otamendi in the build-up — a call the AP described as another that went Argentina's way. It only delayed the inevitable. In the 106th minute Porro crossed from the right, Williams cushioned a header across goal, and Torres — the Barcelona forward sent on to stretch a wilting defence — thrashed his finish past Martinez at last.

The records tumbled with the final whistle. Spain's unbeaten run now stands at 38 matches, surpassing the world record of 37 set by Italy between 2018 and 2021, and they conceded just one goal in the entire tournament — the fewest ever by a World Cup winner. As holders of the European Championship they are now, without argument, kings of both their continent and the world, the first side since their own 2010-12 generation to hold both crowns at once.

For Lionel Messi, 39, there was only heartbreak in what is widely expected to be his last World Cup. He became the first player to start three World Cup finals and the oldest outfield player ever to start one, but he spent the night starved of the ball, shackled by Rodri and Cubarsi, and left the pitch a beaten captain as Spain's players streamed past him towards their supporters.

In Israel, the final was a midnight festival. More than 10,000 fans packed Menora Mivtachim Hall in Tel Aviv for a municipal viewing party — moved indoors from Charles Clore Park after every ticket sold out — watching the drama unfold on giant 360-degree screens with the atmosphere of a home fixture, Israeli media reported. When Torres scored, the basketball arena, more accustomed to Maccabi Tel Aviv's European nights, shook like it does for a buzzer-beater.

The night may also have settled football's next great argument. Lamine Yamal, 19, quiet by his standards yet always threatening, adds a World Cup to a Euro at an age when most players are still waiting for a debut, and Goal.com's power rankings already listed him as the bookmakers' Ballon d'Or favourite before kick-off. The tournament's official verdict followed within the hour: Rodri, Spain's metronome, was named player of the tournament ahead of Messi; Unai Simón took the Golden Glove after a record 650 consecutive minutes without conceding; Pau Cubarsí was voted the best young player; and Kylian Mbappé's ten goals had already sealed the Golden Boot. As Messi's era closed in New Jersey, the succession was standing 30 metres away, wearing the same number ten — for the other side.
facts: Final: Spain 1-0 Argentina after extra time; Ferran Torres scored in the 106th minute (ESPN, FIFA match centre, AP).
Enzo Fernandez was sent off at 90+3 for a second yellow card after a reckless foul on Pau Cubarsi; his first booking came in the 82nd minute for dissent (ESPN, AP, NBC News).
Emiliano Martinez made 11 saves — the most ever recorded in a World Cup final (ESPN, AP via Yahoo Sports).
Spain led possession 65%-35% and shots 20-2 (12-0 on target); Argentina did not register a shot on target (ESPN Gamecast statistics; also per NBC News).
A Nico Williams goal early in extra time was disallowed for a foul on Nicolas Otamendi in the build-up (AP; incident corroborated by Sky Sports).
Spain extended their unbeaten run to 38 matches, breaking Italy's world record of 37 set between 2018 and 2021 (ESPN, AP).
Spain conceded one goal in the entire tournament — the fewest by any World Cup winner (ESPN, AP).
More than 10,000 fans attended the Tel Aviv municipality's viewing party at Menora Mivtachim Hall, relocated from Charles Clore Park after tickets sold out, per Israeli media reports.

Spain swept the individual awards: Rodri the Golden Ball ahead of Messi, Unai Simón the Golden Glove (record 650 consecutive minutes unbeaten), Pau Cubarsí best young player; Kylian Mbappé won the Golden Boot with ten goals (ESPN, Yahoo Sports, Sports Illustrated, Manchester City official).

body: Maccabi Haifa's summer-long goalkeeping saga is all but over. Both halves of the club's planned reshuffle — the sale of Heorhiy Yermakov to Ukrainian side Metalist Kharkiv and the return of Israel international Omri Glazer from Red Star Belgrade — have been agreed, an Israeli sports outlet reported on Sunday evening, with the deals expected to take full effect within 48 hours once all parties have signed contracts.

Glazer, a 30-year-old goalkeeper with 23 senior caps for Israel, has agreed a contract for the next four years, according to the report, which puts the fee due to Red Star Belgrade at an estimated 600,000 dollars. The Serbian champions had initially pushed for the Israeli to stay in Belgrade or command a substantially higher price, but subsequent Israeli reports said the club formally cleared him to leave, with a medical examination among the final steps before signing.

The move would open a second spell at the club for Glazer, who was on Maccabi Haifa's books from 2016 to 2021, a period that included a loan at Sektzia Ness Ziona. He established himself as first choice at Hapoel Be'er Sheva between 2021 and 2023 before joining Red Star Belgrade, where he made more than 50 appearances and played European football. His contract in Serbia had been due to run until June 2027.

Travelling in the other direction, at least figuratively, is Yermakov. Metalist will pay three million euros for the 24-year-old Ukrainian, per the report — a figure broadly consistent with earlier Israeli reporting that described an offer of 2.8 million euros rising to three million through add-on clauses. The goalkeeper, who is said to be tripling his wages in Ukraine, leaves Haifa after a single season.

Kyiv-raised and a product of the Shakhtar Donetsk academy, Yermakov arrived in Israeli football via FC Oleksandriya, where he spent a further season on loan after Haifa acquired his rights, before joining up with the Greens' first team and making over 30 appearances last season. His willingness to move had reportedly been secured earlier in the window, with the two clubs left to close the gap on the fee.

It is worth underlining what has and has not happened: both transfers are agreed rather than officially announced. Neither Maccabi Haifa, Red Star Belgrade nor Metalist has confirmed the deals, and the report frames the coming 48 hours — signatures, paperwork and formal unveilings — as the window in which the agreements become official.

For Haifa, the double deal resolves the position that has dominated their summer and lets the recruitment department move on: having completed the signing of Wanderson Tsunami, a left-sided defender who can also cover at left-back, the club has reportedly turned its search toward a right-footed centre-back as preparations for the new season continue.

body: Jeff Dowtin Jr, the American point guard whose single season at Maccabi Tel Aviv ended with an early parting of ways, is heading to Italy. Napoli Basket officially announced his signing for 2026-27 on Monday, confirming a move Israeli and Italian media had reported as agreed the previous evening.
The move settles a summer of uncertainty for the 29-year-old, who had been in negotiations with AEK Athens before that path closed. Naples, not Athens, will now host his second European season.
Dowtin arrived in Tel Aviv in August 2025 on a three-year contract, his first stop outside North America after NBA spells with Golden State, Milwaukee, Orlando, Toronto and Philadelphia.

His numbers in yellow and blue were respectable rather than commanding: 9.6 points and 4.3 assists in around 21 minutes per game in domestic play, and 8.1 points with 2.4 assists in just over 17 minutes a night in the EuroLeague.
It was not enough to see out the deal. Maccabi and Dowtin agreed to part ways in May, before the season had finished, and the guard re-entered the market.

Napoli represent an ambitious landing spot. The Serie A club return to European competition for the first time in nearly two decades and have been drawn into a EuroCup group featuring Bourg-en-Bresse, Tofas Bursa, Buducnost and Trentino, among others.
For Dowtin, the EuroCup offers a stage a rung below the EuroLeague nights he knew in Tel Aviv — and a chance to run a team of his own in a city rediscovering its basketball appetite.

body: Hapoel Tel Aviv's basketball club confirmed on Sunday that they will begin the coming season outside Israel, telling supporters that, for now, the campaign will open in the Bulgarian capital. "At the moment — we will open the season in Sofia," the club said, extending an arrangement that defined their historic first EuroLeague campaign.

In an official statement — issued in the club's name rather than attributed to any individual executive — Hapoel explained the reasoning in plain terms. "In light of the heating-up of the security situation, and in order to prepare in the best possible way for the coming season, it was decided to maintain activity bases both in Sofia and in Israel," the statement read.

The wording was deliberately provisional. The club said the main activity base will sit in Sofia "at this stage," that it will continue to monitor developments, and that if the security picture in Israel improves, the possibility of moving the principal base back home will be examined. No end date was given, and the club did not specify which competitions, or how many fixtures, the arrangement will cover.

The decision continues rather than begins Hapoel's Bulgarian chapter. Throughout 2025-26 — the club's debut season in the EuroLeague — home games in the competition were staged at Arena 8888 in Sofia, the hall formerly known as Arena Armeec, under the alternative-venue arrangements the league put in place for Israeli clubs while the security situation kept top-tier European basketball from being played in Israel.

That debut campaign was itself the product of a breakthrough: Hapoel earned their EuroLeague place by winning the 2024-25 EuroCup, sweeping Gran Canaria in the final. In their first season among Europe's elite they reached the 2026 playoffs, where they met Real Madrid, before the title was decided in Athens, where Olympiacos were crowned champions.

A squad member, quoted without being named in one of the Israeli reports, suggested the players had been braced for the news. "They said we'd start in Bulgaria and progress from there. There are still security matters, but we're going with whatever the team decides," the player said.

For Hapoel's supporters, the announcement lands as a familiar disappointment: a second consecutive season, at least at its outset, in which the biggest nights of the club's European life will begin some 1,600 kilometres from Tel Aviv. The club's own framing, though, leaves the door conspicuously open — the operative words remain "at the moment," with everything after that contingent on quieter times at home.

body: Hapoel Jerusalem have made an opening bid to bring former Denver Nuggets forward David Roddy to the Israeli capital, offering the 25-year-old American a contract worth approximately $2.2 million over two years, according to a report published in Israel on Sunday evening. Roddy is said to have rejected that first proposal, but the two sides remain in negotiations.

The report, by a named Israeli basketball correspondent, indicates that Jerusalem view the rejection as a step in an ongoing negotiation rather than the end of the pursuit, and that the club is continuing its effort to close a deal. No other outlet has yet confirmed the talks, and neither the club nor the player has commented publicly.

Roddy, a 6-foot-5 forward built more like a linebacker than a wing, was one of the most decorated college players in the country at Colorado State, where he was named Mountain West Player of the Year in 2022. Philadelphia selected him with the 23rd overall pick in that summer's NBA draft before trading his rights to Memphis on draft night.

What followed was a well-travelled four-year NBA career: two seasons with the Grizzlies, a February 2024 trade to Phoenix, a stint in Atlanta, a brief return to Philadelphia on 10-day and two-way deals, a two-way contract in Houston and, this past March, a two-way agreement with Denver. Across 181 NBA regular-season games he averaged 6.3 points and 2.9 rebounds, and per the Israeli report he contributed 8.0 points and 4.0 rebounds in five appearances for the Nuggets last season.

The pursuit fits the shape of Jerusalem's summer. The club has appointed veteran Serbian coach Sasa Obradovic, who led Monaco to the 2023 EuroLeague Final Four, on a contract running through 2028-29, and has formally applied for a two-year EuroLeague license ahead of the shareholders' decision on the 2026-27 field. For now, the team is preparing for another BKT EuroCup campaign.

Domestically, Jerusalem are trying to close the gap on the Tel Aviv powers after a season that ended in frustration: a third-place finish in the Winner League regular season at 18-8 was followed by a semi-final exit against Hapoel Tel Aviv, while Maccabi Tel Aviv went on to claim the championship. The roster rebuild is already under way, with big man Devontae Cacok among the arrivals on a two-year deal.

An outlay in the region of $2.2 million for a single player would signal serious financial ambition by Israeli league standards, and landing a 25-year-old with 181 NBA games behind him would be a statement of intent to match the club's European aspirations. With the first offer rebuffed and talks continuing, the coming days should show whether Jerusalem are willing to raise their bid.

body: Hapoel Haifa's squad flies home from its pre-season camp in Bulgaria on Monday to an unwelcome discovery: according to a report on Sunday evening, the club is currently barred from its Beit Nagler training complex. Haifa Municipality is said to be withholding access over an alleged unpaid debt of thousands of shekels, a decision that lands six days before the club opens its Toto Cup campaign against Maccabi Haifa in the city derby next Saturday.

The story was first reported by a local Haifa outlet before the club issued a lengthy, and unusually bitter, public response — one that did not dispute the existence of a payment question, but attacked the city's treatment of the club root and branch.

"After cutting the annual support budget for Hapoel Haifa to 29,000 shekels — roughly our annual socks budget — the municipality continues to turn a cold shoulder to the club," the club said in the statement. "Unfortunately, we feel like an unwanted, unloved stepchild in the city, to put it mildly."

The statement went further, accusing the city of "failing one of the oldest and most important institutions in the city, in its 103rd year," and of forcing the club "to compete with unequal tools against rivals budgeted in the millions of shekels, including facilities provided free or subsidised by municipalities." The club also questioned the timing, calling the emergence of the ban days before the derby "puzzling."

There is history here, and it is strikingly recent. In the summer of 2025 the same municipality barred the same club from the same Beit Nagler complex over a debt then put at roughly NIS 100,000, saying training could resume once it was settled; the club responded at the time that it pays more than NIS 2 million a year for its use of Beit Nagler and Sammy Ofer Stadium and would settle any bill on formal demand. That episode was resolved; its reappearance a year on suggests a structural rather than incidental problem in the relationship.

What is missing, this time, is the city's side. Haifa Municipality had issued no statement on the fresh bar by Sunday night, and the precise size and age of the debt now claimed has not been confirmed on the record. Until it speaks, the club's furious framing stands alone.

The stakes are immediate either way. The Toto Cup derby against Maccabi Haifa next Saturday is the club's first competitive fixture of the 2026-27 season, and a side that lands from Bulgaria on Monday with its training base in doubt has, at best, a badly disrupted match week. If the last round of this fight is any guide, a payment — and a formal demand for one — would end it quickly.

title: Evenepoel conquers the Solaison as Vingegaard crashes out of the Tour
dek: Remco Evenepoel outkicked Tadej Pogacar and Isaac del Toro on the Plateau de Solaison for his first road-stage win at the Tour de France, on an afternoon overshadowed by Jonas Vingegaard's crash and first career Grand Tour abandonment.

body: Remco Evenepoel climbed to the finest road victory of his Tour de France career on Sunday, winning stage 15 atop the Plateau de Solaison ahead of race leader Tadej Pogacar — but the Alpine afternoon will be remembered as much for what the race lost as for what the Belgian won. Jonas Vingegaard, twice a champion in Paris and lying second overall at the start of the day, crashed on the approach to the final climb and left the race in an ambulance, abandoning a Grand Tour for the first time in his career.

The 183.9-kilometre stage from Champagnole delivered the first summit finish of this Tour's Alpine block: the hors-categorie Plateau de Solaison, 11.3 kilometres at around nine per cent and making its Tour debut. Inside the final kilometre Isaac del Toro launched the expected attack, but Evenepoel matched the young Mexican and then countered decisively, crossing the line ahead of Pogacar with Del Toro third at six seconds, and the next group, including Paul Seixas and Florian Lipowitz, conceding just under a minute.

For Evenepoel, now in his first season with Red Bull-Bora-hansgrohe, it was a breakthrough moment: his previous Tour stage wins had come against the clock, and this was his first at the summit of a mountain, taken toe-to-toe with Pogacar on one of the steepest finishes of the race. With the world time-trial champion refusing to crack on the double-digit ramps, the result reframes the podium battle heading into the final week.

The decisive drama, however, came roughly 21 kilometres from the finish. With Visma-Lease a Bike driving the peloton in pursuit of the breakaway, Vingegaard's front wheel slipped as he exited a roundabout and he went down hard into the kerb, according to reports from the race by Cyclingnews and TOUR Magazin. His teammate Sepp Kuss and UAE Team Emirates-XRG riders Isaac del Toro and Brandon McNulty were also brought down; Del Toro remounted quickly, but the Dane could not continue.

Race doctors treated Vingegaard at the roadside and placed his right arm in a sling before he was taken away in a race ambulance, with international outlets reporting a heavy impact to his shoulder. Visma-Lease a Bike had not published a full medical bulletin by the time the stage finished, and the precise extent of the injury remained unconfirmed on Sunday evening — but the team's withdrawal of its leader ends his bid for a third Tour title in the cruellest fashion.

Vingegaard's exit redraws the general classification. Pogacar, who by several accounts rode in service of Del Toro's podium ambitions rather than chasing the stage himself, retains the yellow jersey — and the polka-dot jersey besides — with Evenepoel moving up to second overall at five minutes and Del Toro third at 5:58, while Mads Pedersen continues to lead the points classification. Monday's rest day now precedes a final week in which the fight is for the podium as much as for yellow.

For Israeli fans, this is the first Tour since the team founded as Israel Cycling Academy stopped down its national identity: the former Israel-Premier Tech now races as NSN Cycling Team under a Swiss licence, owned by the Never Say Never group co-founded by Andres Iniesta, after the protest-scarred 2025 season. Its eight-man Tour squad, built as a sprint train around Biniam Girmay, includes no Israeli riders this year — Israeli champion-in-waiting Nadav Raisberg was left off the roster — and a brutal summit finish like the Solaison was always going to be a day of survival rather than opportunity for the sprint-focused outfit, which The Times of Israel reports is experiencing a far calmer race since the rebrand.

It was Evenepoel's first Tour de France stage win on a road/mountain stage; his previous Tour wins came in time trials.
Jonas Vingegaard (Visma-Lease a Bike) crashed about 21 km from the finish when his front wheel slipped exiting a roundabout; his right arm was placed in a sling and he left the race by ambulance.
The abandonment — reported by Cyclingnews, Reuters, TOUR Magazin and ProCyclingUK — is the first of Vingegaard's Grand Tour career; he had started the day second overall.
Sepp Kuss, Isaac del Toro and Brandon McNulty also came down in the crash; Del Toro remounted and finished third on the stage.
After stage 15, Pogacar leads the general classification with Evenepoel second at 5:00 and Del Toro third at 5:58; Pogacar also holds the mountains jersey and Mads Pedersen the green jersey.

body: Israel's under-20 national team — the reserve side of Israeli basketball — closed out its FIBA U20 EuroBasket on a sour note on Sunday, falling 95-79 to Lithuania in the ninth-place classification game at Arena Stožice II in Ljubljana. The defeat left the young blue-and-whites 10th of the 16 teams in Europe's top division, with Lithuania claiming ninth.

For a half, Israel looked the likelier side to finish inside the top ten. Lithuania shaded a tight opening quarter 19-18, but Israel answered by taking the second 23-20 and went to the locker room in front, 41-39 — a scoreline confirmed quarter by quarter in FIBA's official record of the game.

The match turned decisively after the break. Lithuania piled on 30 points to Israel's 18 in the third quarter and ended it leading 69-59, the first double-digit gap of the contest. The Lithuanians kept pressing in the fourth, stretching the margin to 21 points before Israel trimmed the final deficit to 16.

Gabrielius Jokubauskas did the bulk of the damage for Lithuania with a game-high 31 points on six three-pointers, according to FIBA's official box score — Israeli match reports initially carried 34, which FIBA's page lists as his efficiency rating, not his points. On the Israeli side, FIBA's leaders card credits Yonatan Keller with 16 points, with Oren Sahar also on 16 and leading the game with eight assists; captain Rany Belaga added a team-high eight rebounds in his final game of the tournament.

The loss capped a campaign of real swings in Ljubljana. Israel went 2-1 in Group D — wins over Romania and the Czech Republic around a defeat to host Slovenia — before dropping into the 9-16 classification bracket. There, a lopsided win over Italy guaranteed Israel's place in Division A, Europe's top flight, for next summer, and a 96-74 dismissal of Latvia in the 9-12 semifinal set up Sunday's meeting with Lithuania. Belaga starred in that Latvia game with a 32-point triple-double, which FIBA noted as just the eighth in the competition's history.

It was the first major tournament for the reserve programme's new coaching staff, installed ahead of this summer. A 10th-place finish is a step back from 2025, when Israel's under-20s reached the quarterfinals and ended the championship sixth, and the Israeli match report carried no post-game comment from the bench.

Still, the bottom line for the program is survival at the top table: Israel will play Division A again in 2027, and it leaves Slovenia with a core led by Belaga — newly signed with Hapoel Jerusalem — plus Sahar and Keller, all of whom produced against elite European opposition. Serbia, meanwhile, took the tournament title in Ljubljana.
facts: Final: Lithuania 95, Israel 79 — ninth-place classification game, FIBA U20 EuroBasket 2026 (Division A), Arena Stožice II, Ljubljana, 19 July 2026; confirmed final by FIBA's official game page.

Israel's earlier classification win over Italy secured its place in Division A for 2027.
Serbia won the 2026 FIBA U20 EuroBasket title; the tournament ran 11-19 July in Ljubljana, Slovenia.

body: Ariel Atias, Israel's national record-holder in the decathlon and, in his federation's estimation, the finest all-round athlete the country has produced, is retiring from competition at the age of 27. The Israel Athletics Federation announced on Sunday that Monday's Israeli Championships, at the Givat Ram Stadium in Jerusalem, will be the last meeting of a career that has spanned 16 years.

"I am finishing this chapter with a heavy heart, but a whole one," Atias said in the federation's statement. "Sometimes one of the greatest challenges for an athlete is knowing when the time has come to stop." He added that for 16 years he had been privileged to live his dream in Israeli athletics.

The numbers behind that career are considerable. Atias made some 20 appearances in Israel colours, set eight age-group records, and collected multiple national titles, including back-to-back senior decathlon championships in 2019 and 2020. In 2020, according to the federation, he broke a national decathlon record that had stood for 26 years.

He then raised the bar further. World Athletics lists his national record at 7,343 points, scored on 14 May 2022 at Drake Stadium in Des Moines, Iowa, where he was competing collegiately for Illinois State University at the Missouri Valley Conference championships. His profile also records an indoor heptathlon best of 5,414 points and a 4.85-metre pole vault, both set in Chicago in February 2024.

The decathlon is athletics at its most unforgiving: ten disciplines across two days, rewarding the athlete who is merely excellent at everything over the specialist who is brilliant at one thing. That Atias dominated the event domestically for the better part of a decade, while carrying his career from Israel to the American collegiate circuit and back, explains why the federation's farewell described him as the best combined-events athlete in the country's history.

The goodbye is not a departure. In recent years Atias had already begun coaching alongside his own training, and in September he will formally join the staff of the federation's Academy for Excellence. There, the federation said, he will remain an inseparable part of the athletics family and help shape the next generation of Israeli combined-events athletes.

First, though, there is one final start. "The track may end here, but my path in sport is only changing direction," Atias said. It ends where it should: at the national championships, in front of his own, with the record book still carrying his name.

title: 'He waited for my first mistake': Stav Lemkin looks back on a first season of two halves at Twente

body: Stav Lemkin has closed the book on his first season in the Netherlands with a strikingly candid verdict on how it began. In an interview with Twente's club magazine De Twaalfde Man, the 23-year-old Israel defender said of the coach who gave him his debut: "It was as if the trainer waited for my first mistake, a first chance to take me out. I was not the player he wanted, I think."

The mistrust, Lemkin said, was something he sensed from pre-season onwards, and it surfaced on the opening weekend. Handed his Eredivisie debut away to PEC Zwolle in August, he was substituted at half-time of a 1-0 defeat. The team fared little better than its new signing: three points from the first four league matches left the club bottom-heavy in the table and the board out of patience, and Joseph Oosting was dismissed on 4 September 2025.

Lemkin was careful not to reduce the poor start to one man's decisions. "There were many new players, and at first it was as if we were all individualists," he reflected, describing a dressing room of strangers still searching for a common idea. Even so, he admitted feeling a measure of sympathy for Oosting when the club decided to act.

The change transformed both the team and the defender's place in it. John van den Brom was confirmed as head coach on 15 September 2025, and under the veteran Dutchman the centre-back went from expendable to indispensable, establishing himself as a regular starter and finishing the campaign with 26 league appearances. "After the change, things improved very quickly," Lemkin said, "and you got the feeling that you were playing with your best friends, or with family."

The turnaround carried the club from crisis to a European place, and Lemkin reserved particular warmth for the supporters who filled the stadium through both halves of the season. "The results were good and we are wonderfully supported by our fans. The atmosphere in the stadium is incredible, and they are always clearly present at away matches," he said. "It is nice that we could also make them happy by reaching European football."

The season completes a rapid ascent for the Tel Aviv-born defender, who came through at Maccabi and Hapoel Tel Aviv before joining Shakhtar Donetsk in 2023. After a season back at Maccabi on loan, Twente paid the Ukrainian club a reported fee of around 1.5 million euros in June 2025 to sign him on a three-year contract, and the investment now looks shrewd for a player who has also won ten senior caps for Israel.

For all the vindication of the second half of his season, Lemkin insists the story is not finished, saying he knows he can still improve. His conclusion, though, was unambiguous: "I am really happy here, and glad that I get to play for this club."

body: AEK Athens have submitted an official offer to Hapoel Be'er Sheva for Kings Kangwa, the Zambian international midfielder who powered the club to last season's Israeli championship. Word of the formal bid emerged in Israel on Sunday evening, with two separate reports confirming that negotiations between the clubs are now live and that the Greek side's proposal is the most substantial yet received for the 27-year-old.

The numbers, however, do not yet add up to a deal. The current AEK offer is understood to exceed €2.5 million, while Be'er Sheva's valuation of their player of the season stands at more than €4 million. One assessment in Israel holds that a bid in the region of €3 million could be enough to bring owner Alona Barkat's club to the table, though as matters stand the offer falls short of her demands.

On personal terms, the gap is rather easier to bridge. According to one report, AEK are prepared to pay Kangwa around €700,000 a year, more than double the roughly €300,000 he currently earns in the Negev — the kind of salary jump that tends to concentrate a player's mind once clubs begin talking.

Kangwa arrived in Be'er Sheva in the summer of 2024 from Red Star Belgrade, where he won a Serbian title and tasted Champions League football, for a fee reported at under €1 million. The investment has been repaid many times over: 14 goals and 8 assists in his first season, then 12 goals and 9 assists in the championship campaign that followed, form that earned him the league's player-of-the-season award. He has 46 caps for Zambia.

Nor is AEK's approach the first of the summer. Levski Sofia are reported to have offered €2 million for the midfielder earlier in the window, a bid Be'er Sheva turned aside without ceremony, and one that now looks like the opening move in a market that has steadily warmed.

In Greece, expectations are running higher still. On the podcast Trivela Boys, Kangwa was described as the closest available match for Orbelin Pineda, the playmaker AEK are seeking to replace, with one analyst estimating the eventual fee would land 'in the region of €8 million' — a valuation, it should be said, that belongs to Greek media speculation rather than to anything either club has put on paper, and one that sits well above the figures reported in Israel.

A regulatory clock is ticking underneath the negotiation. Under Article 30.05 of UEFA's Champions League regulations, a player who is fielded in the qualifying rounds may represent another club in UEFA competition only from the league phase onwards. Be'er Sheva open their qualifying campaign against Vikingur on Tuesday — and if Kangwa plays, he would be cup-tied for the rest of the qualifying and play-off phase, unable to line up for AEK against his old club should the two sides meet in the play-off round, as one Israeli report noted on Sunday evening. An unused substitute, it should be said, is not caught by the rule; only minutes on the pitch trigger it.

The timing sharpens everything. Be'er Sheva open their Champions League qualifying campaign this week, and Kangwa is expected to be central to it — which gives the champions every sporting reason to hold firm, and gives their most coveted player a European shop window in which the price may yet climb.

By Monday morning the endgame appeared to be forming, though the picture remained contested. One Israeli report said AEK were expected to improve their offer to roughly €3.8 million and that the deal could be completed within a day — adding that a transfer sealed before Tuesday's qualifier would spare Kangwa the cup-tie — while a second outlet quoted sources at Be'er Sheva insisting negotiations were "not close right now", and reported figures for both the fee and the player's personal terms that differ between publications. Those around the player left little doubt about his own preference: "This is his time to move," his circle was quoted as saying. "Everyone understands this is the offer — we need to let him go." Unless the clubs converge before kick-off in Reykjavik, the champions' player of the season will simply play on.

body: Maccabi Ashdod have appointed Noa Konfino as team manager of their senior basketball squad ahead of the club's return to Ligat Ha'Al, Israel's top division, according to a report published Sunday. Konfino, 27, takes up the post for the 2026/27 season, and the report states she will be the only woman holding the position in the league.

The role of team manager in Israeli basketball is an administrative one, sitting at the hinge between the coaching staff, the players and the league office. It covers the daily logistics of a professional squad — travel, scheduling, registration and matchday operations — and its holder is a constant presence around the team throughout the season.

Konfino arrives from the analytics side of the game. According to the report on Sport 5, she most recently headed the statistics department at Segev Sports, the company that supplies statistical services to the Israeli Premier League and graphics for basketball broadcasts. The same report says her love of the game was formed watching basketball with her late father.

"I am thrilled and delighted to join the Maccabi Rotstein Ashdod family," Konfino was quoted as saying. "The team has made an impressive journey from the National League to the Premier League, and I promise to do everything to be part of the team's success next season."

She joins a club on a steep upward curve. Maccabi Ashdod sealed promotion on June 11, beating Ironi Nahariya 94-83 at home to close out the National League playoff final 3-1, with Robert Turner III scoring 30 points in the clincher. The victory completed a two-year climb from the third tier to the top flight under head coach Dan Katzir.

Women in senior administrative roles around Israeli men's professional basketball remain a rarity, which is what gives the appointment its wider resonance. A second, bylined report on the club's season plans, published later on Sunday, independently confirmed both the appointment and that Konfino will be the only woman serving as team manager in the top flight next season.

Ashdod's preparations for their first top-flight campaign since promotion are continuing through the summer, with the roster taking shape around the core that won promotion. Konfino's hiring adds an experienced basketball operations mind to the back office as the club readies itself for life among Israel's elite.

body: Maccabi Tel Aviv have loaned out six academy players in a single move, sending the group to second-tier partner club Hapoel Kfar Shalem, according to a report published Sunday afternoon by Sport1.

The six are defenders Ron Feldman, Idan Weinberg and Itay Barhoom, together with Rani Rival, Rom Savich and Yoav Junio. All are graduates of the club's youth department and were part of the academy side that won its championship, with several of the group regarded internally as candidates for eventual integration into the senior squad.

Their destination is a familiar one. Kfar Shalem, who compete in the Liga Leumit under coach Noam Shoham, operate as a de facto feeder side for the yellow-and-blues under a cooperation agreement between the clubs, an arrangement Kfar Shalem announced publicly and which channels Maccabi youth graduates into regular senior football in the second division.

The stated purpose of the moves is playing time. Rather than keeping the group in youth or reserve frameworks, the champions want the six exposed to weekly senior competition, with Weinberg the most prominent of the departing players: he has already travelled with the first team for European fixtures and carries squad number 52 on the club's first-team list.

The mass loan fits an established pattern at the club, which routinely farms out young professionals to gain minutes; Transfermarkt currently lists seven other Maccabi players on loan at clubs in Israel, Hungary and Ukraine, among them teenagers Daniel Tishler and Itay Zafrani.

The timing is no accident. Maccabi opened their trophy season on Wednesday with a 3-1 Super Cup victory over Maccabi Be'er Sheva, and the coaching staff are trimming and shaping the squad ahead of the league campaign and European qualification rounds, making a clear runway for the academy group elsewhere the logical step.

Loan durations and any recall or option clauses were not disclosed in the report, and at the time of publication neither Maccabi Tel Aviv nor Kfar Shalem had posted an official announcement of the six moves on their channels; the transfers are therefore attributed to the reporting outlet pending club confirmation.

body: Beşiktaş president Serdal Adalı has publicly accused Mohamed Salah's agent of derailing the Turkish club's pursuit of the Egyptian forward, claiming an initial understanding with the player was in place before the representative sharply raised his financial demands. Speaking to reporters on Sunday, Adalı directed his frustration not at Salah — a free agent since his Liverpool contract expired — but at agent Ramy Abbas.

According to Adalı, Salah was open to the move to Istanbul and went as far as meeting the club's new head coach, Vincenzo Italiano, together with its sporting director, signalling that he wanted to come. It was only after Turkish media reported that the transfer was close to completion, the president said, that the terms changed.

"After we had already reached an initial agreement, because the media published that the deal was close to being finalised, his agent raised his commission demand to inconceivable levels — around 35 percent," Adalı said, in remarks reported by the Israeli outlet ONE. "From our point of view, there is no chance of accepting such percentages. Moreover, we do not think Salah is aware of these sums."

Adalı also denied that outside intermediaries had been involved in the negotiation, insisting the club had dealt only with Abbas directly. The commission figure is, for now, the president's account alone; the agent's side has not confirmed it, and no fee or contract terms have been made public by either party.

Abbas, for his part, has pushed back on any suggestion that a deal exists. "I personally do not know where Mohamed will play next season," the agent said this week, adding that it is not his practice to hold talks with clubs his client would not want to join. Beşiktaş had earlier issued its own statement dismissing reports of a completed transfer as fiction.

Salah's next destination therefore remains genuinely open. Beyond Beşiktaş, the 34-year-old has been linked with Saudi Arabia's wealthiest clubs and with Major League Soccer, where The Athletic has reported a possible move to Sporting Kansas City — a scenario with a distinctly Israeli subplot, as it would make Salah a teammate of Israel international centre-back Or Blorian, who joined the MLS side from Hapoel Be'er Sheva in June.

If Adalı's version holds, the impasse is about the agent's percentage rather than the player's wishes, and talks could yet be revived; if Abbas's denials prevail, the Istanbul chapter may close before it begins. Either way, one of the most decorated forwards of his generation enters late July without a club, and every stated outcome — Turkey, the Gulf, or America — remains conditional on a negotiation that is still visibly unresolved.

body: Dolev Haziza, the former Maccabi Haifa captain who left the club this summer after seven years, is expected to sign for Maccabi Netanya, according to a report published Sunday by the Israeli sports outlet Sport5, which said the gaps between the two sides have narrowed in recent days.

According to the report, Haziza's agent held a meeting with Netanya officials on Sunday, and the club hopes to complete the deal within days — ideally before Tuesday, when Netanya is due to hold its traditional season-opening training session. The club is said to have pushed that opening back by a week in order to finish assembling its squad.

The report is consistent with a steady trail of coverage in the Israeli press over the past month. Netanya's interest was first reported in late June, when the club was said to have opened preliminary talks with the midfielder, and a separate report last week described significant progress after head coach Ronny Levy spoke directly with the player — while noting that gaps over salary still remained at that stage.

Haziza, 31, spent seven seasons at Maccabi Haifa after arriving from Bnei Yehuda Tel Aviv in 2019. Sunday's report credits him with 247 appearances, 43 goals and 41 assists for the Greens, along with three league championships won during Haifa's title run from 2021 to 2023, a period in which he also wore the captain's armband. Last season he scored nine goals and added two assists.

His departure from Haifa was not of his own choosing. Israeli outlets reported earlier this summer that the club informed the attacking midfielder he was not part of its professional plans, and that he initially weighed a move abroad before talks with Netanya gathered pace in recent weeks.

A move to Netanya would carry an element of homecoming: Haziza was born in the coastal city in July 1995. It would also be only the fourth stop of a career that has taken in Bnei Yehuda, a loan spell at Hapoel Ramat Gan and Maccabi Haifa — alongside 18 caps for the Israel national team.

For now, the deal remains unsigned, though the direction of travel is unmistakable. In a conversation with head coach Ronny Levy on Monday morning, Haziza said he was "determined to prove myself" and to show he can still lead a top-flight side, according to a follow-up report — which added that only small financial gaps remain, centred on two constructions for bridging his wages: Maccabi Haifa topping up his first-year salary, or a compensation payment from Haifa before the move. Netanya's management was described as optimistic about completing the transfer within days.
